Baseless Study Proves Nothing of Young Men and Video Games, Despite Rallying Cries of Truth
Okay, so an asshole put a survey on tumblr and claimed it was a school survey? What other outlets are countering this. Is this fraud?
This has been posted on almost every major gaming news site and pretty much treated as fact. It's disgusting.

That's not what happened. A couple of researchers conducted what amounted to a poll of a convenience sample, which they identified as such, which was then picked up by a variety of media outlets who treated it as though it was a proper study.

An aspiring psychologist, freshly educated on the fundamental principles behind the scientific method and, more specifically, scientifically sound and statistically relevant research methodologies, applies their newly stamped knowledge of what does or does not constitute a good research study to point out what this low-level discussion fodder lacked by way of structure that would have made it a truly viable scientific study. Said author makes the mistake of blaming the researchers exclusively, instead of placing appropriate weight on the media's responsibility in misrepresenting the scope and weight of the study.

Gotta read the details. Taking a third-hand summary as gospel only promotes further misunderstanding. The initial study was undertaken for the purpose of promoting discussion, not gathering and presenting any kind of substantive scientific knowledge.

You usually can't even convince someone that their informal poll/tally consisting of 23 samples isn't statistically significant. Barfing science-speak all over an audience and drawing inaccurate conclusions for them is irresponsible. So the author of this article has a role to play in spreading misinformation, as did the media outlets that referenced it as being more than it is. And yes, the researchers have a role to play as well, for not being sufficiently clear that they were presenting a discussion piece, not a proper study.

It's what happens when people have a bias, don't do enough fact checking, and look for what they want to see instead of what is in front of them. It's not fraud unless there was intent to mislead. There is no evidence to support such a claim.

In regards to anything NicheGamer got wrong, leave a comment to them on the article with a source on the accurate information that way they can edit the inaccuracy. I see them edit mistakes that are pointed out to them all the time.

The author of the article himself already pointed out the accurate information. He's the one who indicated where the information was presented and in what context. He just chose to ignore it when it came time to present his point of view.
